Create a realistic vertical indoor lifestyle portrait with the feel of a casual smartphone snapshot. An adult young woman, visually in her twenties, is sitting on the edge of an ordinary residential kitchen counter or low cabinet. Her torso is turned slightly toward frame right, her weight resting naturally on one side of her hips while she curls forward just a little. Both knees are bent and drawn close to her body. Because her legs are much closer to the lens than her face, her thighs and knees become a prominent wide-angle foreground occupying much of the lower frame. Crop the feet naturally rather than forcing the entire body into the composition.

She wears a fitted cream-white or ivory stretch-knit short-sleeve top with a soft low scoop/U neckline that naturally reveals the neck, collarbones and a limited amount of upper chest while keeping the abdomen covered. Preserve small realistic fabric folds around the waist, underarms and seated bends. Pair it with faded light-blue everyday denim shorts, naturally creased by the seated posture without exaggerating her shape.

Both hands extend forward and wrap around a simple transparent cylindrical drinking glass containing a small amount of clear or pale liquid. Her fingernails are muted red or rose pink. A dark brown beaded bracelet sits on one wrist. She wears two layered fine gold-toned necklaces: a shorter one with a small floral/geometric diamond-like pendant and a longer one with a circular decorative pendant.

Her hair is very dark brown-black, close to natural black, pulled back into a loose low bun or low twist, secured at the rear with a dark accessory carrying lighter stripes. Leave long narrow face-framing strands loose on both sides, plus a few small flyaways around the ears and hairline. Do not make the hairstyle perfectly polished.

Her head is noticeably but naturally tilted to one side, creating a slightly uneven shoulder line. Her eyelids are relaxed and her gaze falls just below or beside the camera rather than locking directly onto the lens. Her lips remain softly parted, the corners slightly lifted with a small glimpse of teeth. She looks as though she had just finished saying something or laughing a second ago; right now the smile is still lingering while she keeps holding the glass, and a moment from now she may lift her eyes again and continue responding to the person behind the camera.

Preserve the reference image's natural soft facial proportions and realistic feature relationships rather than replacing the face with any specific celebrity. Use a sheer celebrity-inspired makeup direction common in contemporary East Asian urban fashion: natural dark straight brows, extremely thin soft brown-black eyeliner, muted brown-rose or dusty pink eye shadow, defined yet restrained lashes, almost no aggressive contouring, faint natural rosy blush, and moist coral-pink or muted-rose lips. Keep the foundation sheer enough for pores and subtle skin variation to remain visible.

Skin tone should be light neutral to slightly warm. Clearly render the visible skin of the face, ears, neck, collarbones, limited upper chest, forearms, wrists, hands, fingers, thighs, knees and part of the lower legs. The tactile impression should feel warm, supple, finely textured and slightly velvety with the gentle resistance of real human skin, not porcelain or plastic. Preserve subtle tone differences around the knees, knuckles and backs of the hands.

Photograph it like a close-range smartphone or small compact digital camera shot, approximately 26–35mm full-frame-equivalent. Position the camera around seated eye level or only a few centimeters higher, angled downward about 5–10 degrees. This is not a mirror selfie and no phone should appear in her hands. Place her head in the upper-right portion of the vertical frame while the nearer legs enlarge naturally through perspective. Use an approximately 3:4 portrait ratio. Do not perfectly level or center the composition; allow mild imbalance, crowded foreground legs, cropped feet and other incidental imperfections.

Use real physical warm-white residential lighting rather than abstract cinematic ambience. A broad soft source from slightly above and left of the camera illuminates the forehead, cheeks, collarbones, arms and front planes of the legs. Create wide soft highlights across the thighs and knees, with gentle natural occlusion shadows along the side of the neck, beneath the arms and between overlapping legs. Pale cabinet doors bounce a small amount of warm fill, while a glossy black backsplash absorbs much of the light and allows the skin to separate naturally from the darker background. No artificial rim light, dramatic backlight, colored LEDs or theatrical light beams.

The background is a real, slightly cramped household kitchen: warm ivory cabinet doors with clear vertical seams across the upper half of the image and a broad glossy black backsplash below. A pale rice cooker or small kitchen appliance sits behind her on frame right, while a partially visible metal kettle, pot or cookware appears near the lower-left edge. Allow small pieces of everyday kitchen clutter rather than converting the room into a luxury showroom.

Preserve mild digital noise, limited dynamic range, slightly soft sharpness, tiny areas of motion softness, compression texture, stray hairs, realistic clothing wrinkles and imperfect framing. Keep enough depth of field for the face, hands, glass, legs and kitchen objects to remain recognizable; avoid creamy large-aperture bokeh. The final image should feel as if a familiar person sitting close by casually captured a single unplanned second—intimate, ordinary and slightly imperfect, with the emotional residue of a conversation that has already been going on for a while.

minor, mirror selfie, phone in hand, standing, lingerie, nudity, exaggerated curves, oversized bust, tiny waist, exposed midriff, plastic skin, over-smoothed skin, heavy makeup, studio lighting, rim light, cinematic grading, strong bokeh, fisheye, extra fingers, fused hands, deformed knees, anatomy errors, perfect symmetry, watermark, text, logo.
